author: show-me state times
title: Eight arrested in St. Louis on drug, gun, and immigration charges after task force probe
text:
Eight individuals were arrested on April 29 in St. Louis and surrounding areas on federal charges related to firearms trafficking, cocaine distribution, and illegal re-entry into the United States.
The arrests are part of an investigation by the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), which was established under Executive Order 14159 to combat criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling operations. The HSTF includes agents from multiple federal agencies such as U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Homeland Security Investigations, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, United States Marshal Service, Drug Enforcement Administration, Internal Revenue Service and United States Postal Inspection Service. Prosecution is led by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Missouri.
Those charged include Ivan Said Henriquez-Corea; Jose Edwardo Maldonado-Vargas (also known as Oscar Rodriguez-Lopez); Manuel DeJesus Hernandez-Maldonado; Heber Marcelino Figueroa-Bardales; Edgar Cruz-Ramirez; Thomas Allen Hull; Maria Amabil Hernandez; and Joan Hurtado-Jimenez. The indictment alleges that several defendants conspired to distribute at least 500 grams of cocaine while others are accused of conspiracy to illegally traffic firearms or purchase weapons for individuals who entered the country illegally. Some face additional charges such as possession of a firearm as an illegal alien or illegal re-entry into the country.
A motion seeking detention for Henriquez-Corea states that sales involving cocaine and at least six firearms between late 2025 and March were monitored or recorded by FBI agents. Several suspects are originally from Honduras or Mexico with varying immigration statuses according to court documents cited in detention motions.
The indictment seeks forfeiture of seven pistols and five AR-style firearms seized during the investigation. Authorities emphasize that indictments are accusations only: “Charges set forth in an indictment are merely accusations and do not constitute proof of guilt. Every defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty.”
The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Missouri investigates federal crimes such as terrorism or fraud while enforcing civil rights through collaboration with law enforcement agencies across its jurisdiction according to its official website. The office operates under the Department of Justice using facilities like the Thomas F. Eagleton U.S. Courthouse in St. Louis as noted online.
The office serves a total area covering 49 counties within eastern Missouri according to its official website, working with other entities both to prevent crime and improve quality of life as described online.
